metrics.name: Absolute Importance of a Service
metrics.plain: How many other services call this one.
metrics.high_means: Many services depend on this one, so a breaking change here propagates widely.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher AIS is hypothesised to reduce modifiability: the service is harder to change without coordinating with its callers.
metrics.limitation: Counts declared edges only. A caller that exists in code but never fires at runtime counts the same as one on the hot path. The declared/observed delta is itself the finding, and needs telemetry to compute.

metrics.name: Absolute Dependence of a Service
metrics.plain: How many other services this one calls.
metrics.high_means: The service cannot do its job alone; its availability is the product of its dependencies'.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher ADS is hypothesised to reduce reliability and testability, since more collaborators must be present or mocked.
metrics.limitation: Same declared-only limit as AIS. Also blind to call frequency: one call per request and one call per year count alike.

metrics.name: Absolute Criticality of a Service
metrics.plain: Importance times dependence: services that are both called and calling.
metrics.high_means: The service sits on a path rather than at an end of one, so a failure both affects callers and is affected by callees.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher ACS is hypothesised to concentrate failure impact, making the service a candidate for extra resilience work.
metrics.limitation: A product is zero whenever either factor is zero, so a heavily called leaf service scores 0. That is the intended reading (criticality here means on-a-path, not important) but it is easy to misread.

metrics.name: Service Coupling Factor
metrics.plain: Density of the service graph: what fraction of all possible directed pairs actually communicate.
metrics.high_means: The system tends towards a mesh rather than layers, so no service can be reasoned about in isolation.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher SCF is hypothesised to reduce modifiability at the system level.
metrics.limitation: Sensitive to |S| in a way that makes cross-system comparison delicate: splitting one service into two lowers SCF without changing any real coupling. Directly inherited from the object-oriented Coupling Factor, and inherits its criticisms.

metrics.name: Asynchrony ratio
metrics.formula: ASYNC%(s) = |async edge elements incident to s| / |edge elements incident to s|
metrics.plain: What share of this service's communication is asynchronous rather than a blocking call.
metrics.high_means: The service is temporally decoupled from its collaborators, which usually helps availability and hurts traceability.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher asynchrony is hypothesised to improve availability and complicate debugging and end-to-end latency accounting.
metrics.limitation: Undetermined for a service with no edges, since a ratio over zero edges is not zero. DD-004 governs what may count as async at all: without that rule this metric measures the observability stack instead of the application.

metrics.name: Degree centrality
metrics.plain: How many distinct services this one talks to, as a fraction of how many it could.
metrics.high_means: A hub. It participates in a large share of the system's conversations.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher degree centrality is hypothesised to correlate with change-proneness and with blast radius during incidents.
metrics.limitation: Undirected, so it cannot tell a service everyone calls from one that calls everyone. Normalised by graph size, which makes it comparable across systems but hides absolute scale.

metrics.name: Betweenness centrality
metrics.formula: BTW(s) = sum over pairs of the fraction of shortest paths through s, normalised by (|S|-1)(|S|-2)
metrics.plain: How often this service sits on the shortest path between two others.
metrics.high_means: A broker or a bottleneck: traffic between other services routes through it.
metrics.hypothesis: High betweenness with no replication in the deployment model is the bottleneck smell; it is hypothesised to predict availability incidents.
metrics.limitation: Computed unweighted, because this evidence configuration has no observed call volume. The catalogue asks for volume weighting, so today's value answers a weaker question than the one the catalogue poses, and the profile says so in its note.

metrics.name: Number of endpoints
metrics.plain: How many HTTP endpoints the service exposes.
metrics.high_means: A wide public surface, which usually means the service carries several responsibilities.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher NOE is hypothesised to indicate coarser granularity and lower cohesion.
metrics.limitation: Counts endpoint elements, so two HTTP methods on one route count as two. That is what DD-001's identity scheme forces; the catalogue does not say either way, and a different reading would change every NOE in the dataset.

metrics.name: Number of domain entities owned
metrics.plain: How many persisted domain types the service owns.
metrics.high_means: The service owns a large slice of the domain model, which is the data-side signal of a service doing too much.
metrics.hypothesis: Higher NOD is hypothesised to indicate a bounded context that was drawn too wide.
metrics.limitation: The catalogue asks for aggregate roots; the extractor sees persisted types, which over-counts an aggregate spread over several tables. This is a construct-validity gap, not a bug, and it needs a domain-model-aware analyser to close.

metrics.name: Cyclic dependency
metrics.formula: CYC(s) = 1 if s belongs to a strongly connected component of size > 1, else 0
metrics.plain: Is this service part of a dependency cycle?
metrics.high_means: The services in the cycle cannot be deployed, versioned or reasoned about independently.
metrics.hypothesis: Cycles are hypothesised to block independent deployability, the property microservices exist to buy.
metrics.limitation: A predicate over declared edges. A cycle that only closes at runtime, through a message broker or a shared database, is invisible here. Filtering infrastructure out of the graph (DD-002) can also break a cycle that a full-model view would show.

metrics.name: Shared persistence
metrics.formula: SHARED_DB(s) = 1 if exists p in P(s) shared with another service, else 0
metrics.plain: Does this service share a database with another service?
metrics.high_means: Two services are coupled through their data, so neither owns its schema and neither can migrate alone.
metrics.hypothesis: Shared persistence is hypothesised to be the strongest single predictor of coupled deployments in a microservice system.
metrics.limitation: Evaluated within a vendor, since two vendors' DDL are alternative deployments of one service rather than two live stores. Reports undetermined, never 0, when the snapshot does not identify the store: that case is common and it is where a naive implementation reports a clean bill of health.

metrics.name: God service
metrics.formula: GOD(s) = AIS(s) > t1 and NOE(s) > t2 and NOD(s) > t3
metrics.plain: Is this service too important, too wide and too data-heavy at the same time?
metrics.high_means: A service that concentrates the system's coupling, surface and domain data at once.
metrics.hypothesis: God services are hypothesised to be the dominant source of coordination cost in a microservice codebase.
metrics.limitation: Entirely threshold-dependent, and the thresholds are the part of any smell catalogue reviewers attack first. Currently undetermined on every service, because the AIS threshold could not be derived (see DD-006).

absent.name: PageRank
absent.why_absent: The catalogue defines it as weighted by observed call volume. No subject system is instrumented yet, and an unweighted PageRank is a different metric wearing the same name.

absent.name: Size in lines of code
absent.why_absent: The extractor emits no LOC facts. Adding them is easy; doing it before the JVM analyser lands would mean counting lines with a regex.

absent.name: Service Granularity Index
absent.why_absent: A weighted composite of NOE, NOD and LOC_s. Its weighting is an open decision that the catalogue says not to freeze before a sensitivity analysis, and LOC_s does not exist yet.

absent.name: Nano service
absent.why_absent: Defined as NOE = 1 and LOC_s below a threshold. Blocked on LOC_s.

absent.name: Bottleneck
absent.why_absent: Needs betweenness in the top decile plus replication facts from the deployment model. The deployment model exists; the replication facts do not.

absent.name: Call path length
absent.why_absent: Trace-only. The whole of group B needs distributed tracing, and no subject system is instrumented in this configuration.

absent.name: Chatty communication
absent.why_absent: Defined in terms of CHAT, which is trace-only.
